A1.justification: Both complete 25-page PDFs describe the same SAGE research. Text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison, including content shifted across page boundaries.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAGE evaluations on 18 D4RL tasks, controlled feasibility diagnostics, ablations and computational measurements in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, feasibility diagnostics, ablations and computational measurements in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithms 1–2 and Appendix C retain the same JEPA representation learning, action-conditioned predictor, training losses, prefix-energy filtering and penalized candidate ranking.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 18 D4RL tasks across MuJoCo locomotion, Kitchen, AntMaze and Maze2D. The diagnostic corruption scenarios and Maze2D stress test are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, 12 and 13 retain the same comparator membership within each experiment. MCTD is newly mentioned only in related work; it is not added to any reported experimental comparison.

E3.justification: Preprocessing, train/validation splitting, model configurations, training budgets and evaluation metrics remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices C–D. Both versions retain K = 10, P = 0.8 and lambda = 0.1 for the main SAGE experiments.

E4.justification: The action-corruption diagnostics, Maze2D stress test, hyperparameter sweeps, forward-model ablations and inference-cost analysis are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix D. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report the same 500 evaluation episode seeds per task, standard errors, Welch tests, 95% confidence intervals and 10,000-resample bootstrap analysis. Table 3 and Appendices D.4–D.5 retain the same uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains locomotion averages of 84.4 for SAGE and 82.9 for DV*, and Table 13 retains all scores and reported standard errors.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, energy and selection formulas, and appendix statistical formulas remain unchanged, including Equations (1)–(23). No assumptions, propositions or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution statement and conclusion retain the same claims: SAGE separates feasibility from value, reranks candidates without retraining the base planner, and improves performance across the evaluated domains. The conclusion's page break does not change its content.

C2.justification: Interpretations of energy as a feasibility signal, filtering and diversity trade-offs, accumulated prediction error, and Maze2D ceiling effects are retained. No substantive explanation, applicability qualification or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Appendix A replaces the anonymous.4open.science supplementary-code link with the GitHub repository edluyuan/sage and removes the word 'anonymised'. Implementation details, hyperparameters and hardware disclosures are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish any change to the code itself.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a sentence describing MCTD's integration of Monte Carlo Tree Search with diffusion planning, supported by a new reference to Yoon et al. (2025), Monte Carlo Tree Diffusion for System 2 Planning. The broader positioning of SAGE remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds internship and Microsoft Research support acknowledgments, changes correspondence information, and replaces the preprint notice with ICML/PMLR proceedings information. The related-work sentence and Appendix A wording are limited edits; the overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: The expanded first-page footnote and added text cause limited reflow in the introduction, conclusion and bibliography, including continuation of the conclusion onto page 9. Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–13 retain their content, formatting and placement.

improvement.justification: The added MCTD discussion modestly improves related-work coverage, while the named code-repository pointer and support acknowledgments clarify access information and attribution. These are limited documentation improvements; the method, empirical evidence and scientific conclusions remain unchanged.
